identity.worldRole: The readable standard zombie of the horde: a fair baseline pressure unit that lets players judge route, damage and defensive choices without borrowing the wall-breaking silhouette of a brute.
identity.manufactureContext: A stylized undead body transformed by one stable violet frontier mutation. Biology is always primary; sparse hardened growth expresses a fixed hostile condition without implying adaptive learning, player-built armor, copper repair authorship or mechanical chassis language.
identity.emotionalIntent: Immediately recognizable as a zombie, lightly unsettling and tenacious with a touch of awkward physical absurdity, but never realistic, graphic, tragic or gore-dependent.
identity.technologyLevel: undead biological threat with hardened frontier growth
identity.territoryVisualThesis: A clearly undead violet rôdeur whose head-led hunch, open unequal hands and bent shamble receive construction-toy clarity without becoming a toy robot, mascot or fortress module.

instantRead.oneSecondPromise: A hunched violet zombie with a visible face, reaching unequal arms and a broken-crown shoulder bloom advances toward the fortress and shows weakening through posture before color.
instantRead.orientationCue: The bowed zombie head, dark face cavity, forward jaw and reaching arm lead the hunched body; the violet bloom sweeps from one side of the crown toward the opposite shoulder and never reads as a visor.
instantRead.interactionCue: No friendly socket, complete ring, service panel or repair affordance exists; the face and hands are target cues, not interaction controls.
instantRead.dangerCue: A forward cranial profile, open reaching hands, bent pursuit posture and a short pre-swipe draw-back communicate attack intent without giant fists or weapon props.
instantRead.relationToPlayer: A hostile but fair baseline zombie whose facing, swipe preparation, stagger and collapse support immediate recognition, causal combat reading and honest post-failure understanding.

proportionRules: The hunched pear-shaped torso occupies roughly forty-two percent of total height and remains narrower than a brute.
The cranial mass occupies sixteen to twenty percent of total height and projects forward by roughly fifteen percent of body depth.
Arms are thick enough for horde readability but hands remain medium, open and smaller than the head so the unit never promises wall-breaking force.
Bent legs occupy roughly one third of total height and preserve a clear gap between the feet at mobile distance.
The asymmetrical violet bloom stays inside the two-and-a-half-stud width and cannot become a horn, backpack, armor plate or second head.
